title: Always-on-Top World Clock for Windows 11 & 10: Free, Offline
description: Keep multiple time zones above every window. Free open-source world clock for Windows 11 and 10: converter, meeting planner, no ads or telemetry.

mainEntity.name: Is Open World Clock really free?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. There is no price, no ads, no account, and no in-app purchase. It is open source under the MIT License. Tips on Ko-fi are optional and change nothing in the app.

mainEntity.name: Does the always-on-top window work offline?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The whole app works offline. Time zone rules ship with the app, and updates bring new rules when a country changes its clocks.

mainEntity.name: Why does Windows say Windows protected your PC?

acceptedAnswer.text: The installer and the portable exe are not code-signed yet, so SmartScreen may warn you the first time. Select More info, then Run anyway. The Microsoft Store build is signed by Microsoft and does not show this warning.

mainEntity.name: Can the browser version stay on top?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The web demo on the home page is handy for a quick check, but staying above other apps is a feature of the Windows desktop app.
